FAQ.title: Frequently Asked Questions
FAQ.q1: What is the difference between Paper-Based and Computer-Based IELTS?
FAQ.a1: The test content and scoring do not change, but delivery affects navigation and writing. Our PC practice is designed around the computer-delivered format so you can build useful screen habits.
FAQ.q2: How much does IELTS cost and how can I pay in Algeria?
FAQ.a2: The standard Academic or General Training fee is currently 40,000 DA (One Skill Retake is listed at 25,000 DA). British Council Algeria lists online bank-card payment, digital banking, bank transfer, and HSBC cash deposit (with 1% cash stamp duty). Complete payment within 72 hours.
FAQ.q3: Is this course suitable for complete beginners in English?
FAQ.a3: No. This intensive preparation is strictly for candidates with at least an intermediate level (B1/B2). We focus on exam strategy and scoring criteria, not basic grammar.
FAQ.q4: How do your class groups protect individual learning progress?
FAQ.a4: Strictly 8 seats per cohort. The small group allows line-by-line essay correction and personalized speaking feedback from Amine Senouci.
FAQ.q5: Can I join if I am facing an imminent Capago or TLScontact deadline?
FAQ.a5: Yes, if the schedule fits, but no course can guarantee a score by a visa deadline. We first compare your current level, target score, test type, and available preparation time.
FAQ.q6: What does the 5,000 DA first-cohort price cover?
FAQ.a6: Approximately one month of small-group IELTS preparation in Bir El Djir, Oran, covering all four skills in a traditional classroom setting for this introductory cohort, with individual Writing and Speaking feedback. We confirm the timetable before enrolment.
FAQ.q7: When does the Lab open, and does applying reserve a seat?
FAQ.a7: First-cohort applications close on 26 November 2026. Applying is free and does not reserve a seat; we contact applicants with the confirmed timetable and enrolment details.
